Subject: Granular slab mapping + location index for offer approvals

Team —

I attached an initial draft (20260809_slabs_location_index.xlsx) that attempts to do two things we keep hearing in hiring syncs:

1) Move from coarse geo multipliers (US / EMEA / APAC) to a locality index at city/metro level (a 0–200 index where SF = 150, NYC = 140, Remote US smaller metros ~95).
2) Replace a single band-wide ceiling with a slab mapping per level+role bucket so hiring managers have narrower offer ranges and we reduce negotiation variance.

Why this helps: our current offers span too widely at L4–L6 because managers apply a flat +X% for location. A location index + slab ceilings gives predictable ceilings while preserving flexibility at the lower percentiles for strong candidates.

Key asks: please review and respond on the following by EOD Wed (11 Aug):
- Are the proposed slabs per level reasonable? (column: "proposed_slab_ceiling")
- Is the locality index mapping consistent with your expectation for West/East/EMEA hubs?
- Any objections to a pilot scope: US West (SF/Seattle/San Jose metro) + UK (London) + Remote US small metros.

I copied Hannah from MarketBench — she provided a short market methodology for the locality index and a market percentile table (we requested 60th percentile by default, adjusted by role scarcity). She'll be a useful voice for methodology questions.

Attachments: 20260809_slabs_location_index.xlsx, mav_calculation_notes.pdf

Thanks —
Sean

Sean —

Thanks for pulling this together, really useful starting point. A few clarifying notes inline and attached a small pivot (comp_anchors_v2.xlsx) with alternative anchor points:

- Slab ceilings: the L3–L5 slabs look tight (good) but L6 has a wide ceiling in your draft. Suggest we split the L6 slab into L6A / L6B (technical IC vs. manager) with a 6% delta.
- Locality index: looks fine for main metros. For London, can we use a 125 index rather than 130? That better matches our recent offer history.
- Pilot: agree with US West + UK, but add Seattle to the pilot explicitly (we get more hires there than the spreadsheet suggests).

One process question: how do we want Finance involved? We need a quick cost-impact model for the next 12 months (projected uplift if we move to 60th pct baseline + locality uplift). If Finance wants the pivot table, I can send them the comp_anchors_v2 sheet.

No blocker from People Ops side on principle. If we implement the slabs we should also bake the slabs into Offer Templates in Greenhouse (happy to own the GH side once we lock the numbers).

-L

Sean / team —

Quick note on methodology (MarketBench):
- Data sources: Levels.fyi, public job-posting compensation, and a de-duplicated sample of 12 enterprise customers' offers (anonymized).
- Locality index: city-level cost and market pay combined (50/50 weighting), normalized so that US national median = 100.
- Recommended default percentile: 60th. For "scarce" roles (infra, model infra, SRE), we recommend using 70th.
- Calculation notes: see mav_calculation_notes.pdf for the formula used to compute the Market Adjustment Vector (MAV).

Practical notes: for pilots we typically see the largest change in offer value for SF / London (10–18% uplift depending on baseline). For smaller metros the change is within +/-2–3%.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk the group through the MAV calculation if helpful.

—Hannah
MarketBench
